title: Deterministic Sampler & Loadbench Runbook
content:
Purpose
This runbook documents an approach weve been iterating on for repeatable profiling at scale: a deterministic sampling layer plus a synthetic loadbench harness. Goal is to make profiling runs reproducible, reduce noise in tail-latency investigations, and make CI checks that catch regressions in serving runtime scheduling, KV cache hot paths, and kernel-bound token generation hot loops.

Why deterministic sampling?
- Traditional probabilistic sampling (perf/random) yields different call stacks per run; hard to triage small regressions.
- Deterministic sampling pins a seed for workload generation and for which requests get full traces vs lightweight counters, enabling nearly byte-for-byte comparable traces across runs.
- Combined with synthetic workload generators we can force specific distributional shapes (spiky vs steady), long-context vs short-context, and cold-cache vs hot-cache runs.

Key components in this folder
1) benchfarm.py (synthetic loadbench harness) - Python script that: seeds RNG, replays a corpus, injects jitter patterns, and coordinates collectors.
2) deterministic-sampler.go - small Cgo-enabled daemon that attaches to runtime process and toggles perf/eBPF sampling windows based on a seed schedule.
3) collect-and-merge.sh - wrapper that runs perf/eBPF + runtime logs, normalizes timestamps, and emits a merged timeline.
4) ci/bench-ci.yml - GitHub Actions job template used by perf CI.
5) notes/trace-policy-matrix.md - quick reference for which sampling policy to use for which investigation type.

Quick operational workflow
1) Pick the target commit / model variant and note model hash and build id.
2) Checkout the deterministic bench branch: git checkout bench/deterministic-sampler.
3) Prepare the machine: disable turbo, set CPU governor to performance, pin CPUs with taskset; ensure latest perf and bcc packages.
4) Start the serving runtime with the test model and enable KV cache stats: export REDWOOD_KV_STATS=1.
5) Launch benchfarm with a seed and policy name: python3 benchfarm.py --seed 2411 --policy tail-spike-hotcache --duration 900 --collectors perf,ebpf,trace
   - Benchfarm will generate a deterministic sequence of requests and mark which request ids are flagged for full stack capture (based on seed).
6) After run finishes, run collect-and-merge.sh --seed 2411 --out merged-2411.folded to produce flamegraph inputs.
7) Compare with baseline: scripts/diff-flamegraphs.py baseline.folded merged-2411.folded --threshold 0.05

Policies (short)
- baseline-throughput: no tracing, lightweight counters, used for capacity / throughput checks.
- tail-spike-hotcache: reproduce 99.9th latency spikes when KV caches are primed; sample 1-in-500 requests fully, deterministic seed.
- cold-cache-warmup: clears KV cache every N requests, measures early-token generation kernels.
- kernel-dominant: pins more perf sample time and increases eBPF stack depth to capture syscalls and kernel stacks.

Example benchfarm invocation (full)
- python3 benchfarm.py --seed 4096 \
    --corpus corpora/long-context-rails.jsonl \
    --qps 120 --burst 8 --duration 1200 \
    --policy kernel-dominant --collectors perf,ebpf --affinity 2-15

Deterministic sampler behavior (high level)
- Accepts seed and policy. From seed it derives: request-selection-bitmask (which n-th requests to fully sample), jitter schedule, and occasional "stress windows" where QPS doubles for a short window.
- Exposes a tiny HTTP control plane (127.0.0.1:9093) used by benchfarm/CI to arm/disarm sampling and to fetch the current sample-window map.
- Runs as unprivileged for safety; when perf/eBPF is required, the wrapper (collect-and-merge.sh) runs briefly with sudo to collect kernel stacks.

Collector integration notes
- perf: use perf record -F 997 -g --call-graph dwarf -p <pid> for sample-heavy policies. Output -> perf.data then perf script --no-children > stacks.txt.
- eBPF (bcc/trace): attach uprobe to token generation entrypoints and sample syscall durations; for deterministic mode set sample rate low and use benchfarm-provided request IDs to annotate events.
- runtime tracing: our runtime already emits per-token micro-timestamps when REDWOOD_TRACE=1. The collector normalizes those to monotonic offsets.

CI job template (excerpts)
- bench-ci.yml (simplified)
  name: perf-bench-deterministic
  on: [workflow_dispatch, pull_request]
  jobs:
    perf-bench:
      runs-on: self-hosted-perf
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        - name: Build runtime
          run: make build-runtime
        - name: Start runtime with test model
          run: ./build/runtime --model test-mini --port 34567 &
        - name: Run deterministic bench
          run: |
            sudo ./ci/collect-and-merge.sh --seed ${{ github.run_id }} --duration 600 --policy tail-spike-hotcache
        - name: Upload artifacts
          uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
          with:
            name: perf-results-${{ github.run_id }}
            path: perf-artifacts/*.folded

Interpreting diffs and thresholds
- We use script diff-flamegraphs.py to compute relative changes in inclusive samples per stack. Small regressions (<3%) considered noise for single-run; repeat 3 times with different seeds before filing bug.
- For kernel-heavy diffs, normalize by total kernel samples to avoid userland churn dominating results.

Repro tips when traces diverge
- Confirm seeds and policy are identical. Small mismatch in seed encoding (little vs big endian) is a frequent source of non-reproducibility.
- Verify machine topology: different CPU microcode or SMT on/off changes perf behavior. Add machine fingerprint to artifact metadata.
- For intermittent tail issues, run sequence: 1) cold-cache with full sampling, 2) hot-cache with targeted sampling, 3) long steady-state run to catch convoy effects.

Sanity checklist before filing a regression
- [ ] At least 3 runs with different seeds show same top-3 stack increases.
- [ ] Baseline build and candidate build used identical kernel and perf versions.
- [ ] No external network flakiness (use captive test net or localhost for critical runs).
- [ ] Logs merged and timestamps normalized.
- [ ] Artifact uploaded to the PERF bucket with metadata: seed, commit, machine-fingerprint.

Open work / TODOs
- Make deterministic-samplerctl expose an HMAC-signed runfile to prevent accidental cross-tenant sampling. (Marcus)
- Add a GPU-side sampler for token-kernel hotspots (Ava).
- Integrate benchfarm with chaos-injector to toggle NIC queue lengths mid-run for more realistic tail noise. (Diego)

Notes to self / gotchas
- When comparing perf stacks between architectures (ampere -> graviton) you must run an ABI normalization; pointer-size differences change inline frame layout.
- Flamegraph folding: prefer our custom stack-fold format which includes markers for "kv-lookup" and "token-gen" frames to aid automated diffing.
- Avoid using --call-graph fp for libunwind-only builds; DWARF gives more stable stacks for our JITed code.

References and shortcuts
- benchfarm.py (in this dir) -- lightweight harness used in experiments
- scripts/diff-flamegraphs.py -- computes per-frame deltas and highlights >5% regressions
- ci/bench-ci.yml -- action template
- Slack: #perf-investigations, thread: "deterministic-sampler experiment log"

If youre running this for the first time ping @Sophie (owner) or @Diego for a quick walkthrough.
